pathway.title: MURPHY OIL CORP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the company's leverage is low and has fallen even though debt rose. Total debt was USD 1,385.1 million at December 31, 2025 and USD 1,634.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 249.3 million from a USD 500.0 million notes issue, a USD 83.9 million finance lease and the repayment of USD 227.5 million of notes and the USD 100.0 million revolver draw, while calculated EBITDA rose from USD 1,394.0 million (FY2025) to USD 1,837.5 million (LTM Q3 2026), so total debt over EBITDA moved from 0.99x to 0.89x [CP-1 Debt stack; Chart data: leverage]. The management-basis cross-check gives 0.92x on adjusted EBITDA attributable to Murphy of USD 1,784.8 million.

Second, the improvement is a price result. Revenue from production rose to USD 2,507.9 million for nine months 2026 from USD 2,076.8 million, with realized prices up about a third and production down 3 percent, and lease operating costs fell on lower Gulf of America workovers, which management itself describes as partly offset by activity elsewhere [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model: Cost structure; Management explanation of costs]. Part of the cost gain may not repeat, and none of the price gain is protected, because crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and there were no commodity derivatives at September 30, 2026.

Third, free cash flow is modest. Calculated free cash flow (operating cash flow less property additions and dry hole costs) was USD 184.6 million for nine months 2026, which after USD 150.5 million of dividends and USD 21.2 million of distributions to the minority holder of MP Gulf of Mexico, LLC leaves USD 12.9 million; management's own adjusted free cash flow was negative USD 32.2 million for the same period, excluding the minority share [CP-1 Free cash flow and shareholder distributions]. Cash still rose by USD 123.1 million because operating cash flow exceeded investing outflow by USD 155.9 million, while financing used USD 32.8 million.

Fourth, maturities and liquidity are comfortable. No note matures until May 2029 (USD 117.6 million), followed by USD 600.0 million in October 2032, USD 500.0 million in February 2034 and USD 339.8 million in December 2042; the USD 2.0 billion revolver matures January 2, 2031 and is undrawn apart from USD 0.4 million of letters of credit [CP-1 Chart data: debt maturities; Liquidity]. The 2026 refinancing moved the company from a revolver and shorter notes to this profile.

Fifth, claims outside the debt figure are large. Asset retirement obligations are USD 1,065.4 million, operating lease liabilities USD 653.8 million, and net pension and retiree medical liabilities were USD 195.8 million at December 31, 2025, before commitments of USD 1,648.0 million at that date and a new drillship agreement of about USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross from the first quarter of 2027 [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Adding the first three to total debt gives USD 3,549.3 million, or 1.93x calculated LTM EBITDA (see Calculations).

Sixth, creditor protections are unverified. The previous revolver's tests were a maximum leverage ratio of 3.25x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.50x before an investment grade ratings date, and a 60 percent maximum debt to total capitalization after it; the amended facility's terms, the indentures and the ratings are not supplied, and which test applies is unknown [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; CP-0 Gaps]. The mechanical distance to the stated levels is wide (see Calculations) but is not covenant headroom.

cells.text: Global oil and natural gas exploration and production company with onshore and offshore operations; produces crude oil, natural gas and NGLs mainly in the United States and Canada and explores in targeted areas worldwide; E&P segments are United States, Canada and all other countries, plus Corporate; the US refining and marketing business was separated in 2013
Pure upstream exposure with no downstream offset: revenue and cash flow follow commodity prices and volumes

Gulf of America: rights to about 556 thousand gross acres, about 65 percent of 2025 US hydrocarbon production, about 91 percent of Gulf output from ten fields; Eagle Ford Shale: about 130 thousand gross acres and about 35 percent of 2025 US production
Offshore output depends on a small set of fields and on natural decline; onshore is the shorter-cycle offset

Tupper Montney (100 percent working interest, about 139 thousand gross acres), Kaybob Duvernay (70 percent working interest), and non-operated Hibernia (6.5 percent), Hibernia South Extension (4.3 percent) and Terra Nova (18.0 percent) offshore Newfoundland and Labrador
Gas-weighted onshore volumes and non-operated offshore oil add diversification, but operators control Canada offshore uptime

Côte d'Ivoire: five offshore blocks, 1.4 million gross acres, 90 percent (four blocks) and 85 percent working interest; Vietnam: operator with 65 percent (Blocks 144 and 145) and 40 percent (Blocks 15-1/05 and 15-2/17); Brunei 8.051 percent; Brazil blocks; Morocco block at 75 percent working interest signed January 2026, no firm well commitments in the initial three-year phase
Growth options are discretionary spend with dry-hole risk; acreage expiries in 2026 include 4,267 thousand net acres in Vietnam and 558 thousand in Côte d'Ivoire (10-K page:13)

Q3 2026 production excluding NCI 186,495 BOEPD: onshore about 125,400 (34 percent liquids), offshore about 61,100 (88 percent liquids); Tupper Montney 76,000 BOEPD from 200 BOPD of oil. Including NCI, Q3 2026 was 192,283 BOEPD, down from 206,936 in Q3 2025, and nine months 2026 was 182,494 BOEPD against 189,035
Gas volumes are large in BOE terms but earn little revenue: Canada onshore gas was 69.7 of 849.2 million dollars of Q3 2026 revenue
Nine months 2026 revenue from sales to customers 2,507.9 million dollars: crude oil and condensate 2,158.6, NGLs 66.7, natural gas 282.6; Q3 2026: 731.0, 25.9 and 92.3 of 849.2
Oil share of 86.1 percent (nine months, calculated) makes oil price the dominant revenue driver

Nine months 2026: United States 1,997.9 million dollars, Canada 507.1, Other 2.9; United States offshore revenue by product sums to 1,259.7 million dollars; United States share 79.7 percent, United States offshore 50.2 percent, Canada 20.2 percent (calculated)
Revenue is concentrated in United States offshore and onshore oil

Revenue is "largely index-based with price adjustments for floating market differentials"; Canada onshore gas contracts include floating index pricing and fixed-price physical forward sales. Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 realized prices: United States onshore crude 86.48 against 65.48 dollars per barrel, United States offshore 89.38 against 67.00, Canada offshore 108.21 against 69.42; Canada onshore gas 1.63 against 1.22 dollars per thousand cubic feet
Oil prices rose about a third year on year (32.1 percent onshore, 33.4 percent offshore, calculated); gas realizations in Canada stay low

WTI crude futures were 89.42 dollars per barrel at September 30, 2026 and 104.12 dollars at the end of October 2026, which the company describes as a 16 percent increase; the forward curve for the rest of 2026 was 96.46 dollars per barrel at November 2, 2026
Current earnings reflect a high-price period; a price reversal would lower cash flow with little offset

No commodity-based derivative contracts were in place at September 30, 2026. Fixed-price forward gas sales in Canada: 59 MMCF per day at C$3.00 for October to December 2026 and 9.5 MMCF per day at C$3.14 for 2027, accounted for as normal sales
Oil is unprotected; the gas forward sales cover a small share of Canadian volume (about 59 of 464 MMCF per day of Q3 2026 Canada onshore gas, calculated)

Nine months 2026 against nine months 2025 (million dollars): lease operating expenses 436.4 against 605.0; DD&A 787.9 against 736.9; transportation, gathering and processing 139.4 against 151.1; exploration 155.2 against 57.4, of which unsuccessful exploration well costs and previously suspended exploration costs were 86.7 against 0.1; selling and general 114.1 against 98.7. Lease operating expense per BOE excluding NCI 8.56 against 11.46 dollars
Falling operating cost per barrel supports margin; rising exploration and DD&A offset part of it

Management attributes lower lease operating expenses to "substantially lower workover and production-related costs in the Gulf of America, partially offset by higher activity in the Eagle Ford Shale" and higher exploration expense to dry hole costs in Côte d'Ivoire and Vietnam
Workover swings can reverse; treat the cost fall as partly non-recurring until repeated

Nine months 2026 property additions and dry hole costs 1,333.0 million dollars; capital expenditures attributable to Murphy 1,363.2; 2026 guidance 1,500 to 1,600 million dollars excluding NCI, with 190 million dollars in Q4 2026. Development spending: Gulf of America 447.8, Eagle Ford Shale 232.2, Tupper Montney and Kaybob Duvernay 128.1, Vietnam 99.4; exploration expenditures 471.0 million dollars
Spending is a large share of operating cash flow and is partly discretionary, which is the main lever if prices fall

Proved reserves 730.0 million BOE at December 31, 2025, of which 311.1 million BOE (43 percent) is undeveloped and 15.0 million BOE is attributable to the NCI; 2025 production 68.9 million BOE; 2025 spend to convert undeveloped reserves about 690 million dollars; expected 450 to 800 million dollars per year over the next three years
Reserve life is about 10.6 years of 2025 production (calculated); converting undeveloped reserves requires sustained capital

Net working capital liability of 57.2 million dollars at September 30, 2026 against 246.0 million dollars at December 31, 2025; receivables rose 112.5 and payables rose 50.6 million dollars, which management links to higher oil and NGL prices and Gulf of America drilling
Working capital is a small liability; price rises tie up receivables
Many purchasers in the markets where Murphy produces; no customer concentration percentage and no major-customer disclosure found
Missing datapoint: share of revenue from the largest purchasers; it matters for counterparty and offtake risk

Murphy reports 100 percent of MP GOM with a 20 percent NCI; formed under a Contribution Agreement dated October 10, 2018 among Murphy Exploration & Production Company - USA, Petrobras America Inc. and MP GOM (exhibit list). NCI net income 71.4 million dollars and distributions 21.2 million dollars in nine months 2026 against 43.2 million dollars distributed in nine months 2025

Part of Gulf of America cash flow leaves to the minority holder (the NCI took 13.5 percent of consolidated nine-month 2026 net income, calculated); the holder's identity is not stated in the text read

August 2026 produced water release from a pipeline on private land in Tupper Montney West, reported to authorities and under remediation; higher other operating expense of 28.6 million dollars in Q3 2026 against 5.9 million dollars was attributed to abandonment and environmental remediation costs in the Gulf of America and Canada
Remediation and abandonment costs are recurring operating items; the release amount is not stated
CEO quote: "this breadth of capabilities is what differentiates Murphy"
Promotional; not adopted as evidence of resilience

runs.text: Strengths. Low leverage is a documentary result: total debt is USD 1,634.4 million against calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million, and net debt is 0.62x (Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the characterisation) [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 2,499.9 million of cash and undrawn capacity, a revolver to January 2031 and no note before May 2029 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity; Chart data: debt maturities]. Operating cash flow was USD 1,517.6 million for nine months 2026, 52.0 percent above nine months 2025, and calculated LTM EBITDA covers interest paid 21.29x (Documentary Fact for the cash flow, Analyst Interpretation for the cover) [CP-1 Calculations]. Asset base: proved reserves of 730.0 million barrels of oil equivalent at December 31, 2025, about 10.6 years of 2025 production, spread across Eagle Ford Shale, Gulf of America, Tupper Montney, Kaybob Duvernay, Canada offshore and Vietnam, with 43 percent undeveloped (Documentary Fact for reserves, Analyst Interpretation for diversification) [CP-1A Company and operating model: United States assets; Canada assets; Reserves and replacement]. Capital allocation flexibility: buybacks fell from USD 301.4 million in 2024 to USD 102.6 million in 2025 and USD 0.8 million in nine months 2026, which favors creditors, and no related-party leakage, creditor-adverse transaction or sponsor is documented (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading) [CP-1A Governance, capital allocation and disclosure behaviour]. Disclosure quality: quarterly reconciliations of non-GAAP measures and a covenant compliance statement each quarter (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance].

Weaknesses. Unhedged oil exposure: crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and no commodity derivatives were in place at September 30, 2026; a 10 percent lower oil price on nine-month volumes would have cut revenue and EBITDA by about USD 215.9 million, or 14.0 percent of nine-month calculated EBITDA, before any cost offset (Documentary Fact for the exposure, Analyst Interpretation for the arithmetic) [CP-1A Hedging; Revenue streams]. Thin cash cushion after investment and dividends, as described above (Documentary Fact for the amounts) [CP-1 Free cash flow]. Concentration and decline: United States offshore supplies 50.2 percent of nine-month revenue, and production including the minority share fell 7 percent in Q3 2026, mostly on Gulf of America volumes (Documentary Fact for the percentages, Management Language for the cause) [CP-1A Geographic revenue mix; Volume and mix]. Discretionary, high-risk spending: exploration expense was USD 155.2 million for nine months 2026, including USD 86.7 million of unsuccessful well costs, and the drillship agreement adds a contracted element from 2027 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Cost structure; Transaction summary]. Claims outside debt, including asset retirement obligations equal to about 65 percent of total debt (Analyst Interpretation, calculated) [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Unverified creditor terms: covenants, indentures, ratings, ownership percentages and customer concentration are missing (Insufficient Information; each missing datapoint is listed under Gaps) [CP-0 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps]. Perimeter: the minority holder takes a share of Gulf of America cash flow, 13.5 percent of consolidated nine-month 2026 net income, and releases and filings use different perimeters (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model: MP GOM subsidiary].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no acquisition, buyout, sponsor transaction or restructuring in the sources and none in the run context, so the transaction row is Insufficient Information by design: no transaction source exists, and nothing is invented. The relevant transactions are financings and asset-level events, each stated with its status as of the cutoff.

Financing, completed: on January 2, 2026 the company amended its credit agreement to a 2.0 billion dollar senior unsecured guaranteed revolving facility maturing January 2, 2031, with 12.3 million dollars of transaction costs, replacing the previous 1.35 billion dollar facility maturing October 7, 2029; on January 23, 2026 it closed a public offering of 500.0 million dollars of 6.500% senior notes due February 15, 2034 with 8.3 million dollars of costs, using the proceeds to repurchase and repay debt and fees and for general corporate purposes; in the first quarter of 2026 it redeemed the remaining 78.9 million dollars of 5.875% notes due 2027 and 148.6 million dollars of 6.375% notes due 2028, 227.5 million dollars in total at a cost of 3.5 million dollars, and repaid the 100.0 million dollar revolver draw outstanding at December 31, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:14-15; 10-K page:113-114). Earlier, in October 2024, it closed 600.0 million dollars of 6.000% notes due 2032, used to fund tenders and repurchases that the 10-K describes as a debt-neutral transaction (10-K page:114). Net effect on liquidity: the revolver commitment rose by 650.0 million dollars and cash plus undrawn capacity was 2,499.9 million dollars at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 handoff). A shelf registration permits further offerings through October 15, 2027.

Lease financing, completed: in Q3 2026 a finance lease commenced for the Lac Da Vang floating storage and offloading vessel, September 2026 to October 2039, with a right-of-use asset of 103.4 million dollars and a lease liability of 83.9 million dollars (10-Q Q3 page:32). This is a new debt-like claim of the kind that lease financing creates outside the notes.

Pending or subsequent, within the cutoff: in October 2026 the company agreed to use a deepwater drillship in the Gulf of America for an initial ten wells at approximately 225 million to 325 million dollars gross, with options for up to five more wells, expected to start in the first quarter of 2027 and not recognized at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:32); it secured six exploration blocks from the August Gulf of America lease sale and signed agreements with Mauritania for two offshore blocks, and is working to finalize an agreement in Cameroon before year-end (10-Q Q3 page:34, page:52). In January 2026 it signed a Petroleum Agreement for a 75 percent working interest in a Moroccan deepwater block (10-K page:4-5). These are exploration commitments of unquantified size beyond the drillship.

Asset transactions in the history: purchase of the Pioneer floating production storage and offloading vessel from BW Offshore (UK) Limited for a gross price of 125.0 million dollars in the first quarter of 2025, with a five-year operations and maintenance contract that began in 2025; a 23.0 million dollar purchase of additional Eagle Ford Shale working interest in the third quarter of 2025; and, in 2023, sales of part of the Kaybob Duvernay working interest and the entire 30 percent non-operated working interest in the Placid Montney (10-Q Q3 page:13; 10-K page:5-6). The text read does not describe the terms of the 2023 sales.

New debt issue summary: the only new notes in the period are the 6.500% notes due 2034 (500.0 million dollars). No sponsor, use-of-proceeds dispute, rating action or market quote is in the sources; the instruments' security, guarantors and covenants are not printed in the notes read and the indentures are not supplied (see Gaps).

fields.value: The financial base is sufficient for a credit snapshot of MURPHY OIL CORP, with stated restrictions. Evidence: the audited FY2025 statements and the unaudited Q1 to Q3 2026 statements are complete and tie to the debt note (total debt 1,634.4 million dollars at September 30, 2026 equals current maturities of 11.229 plus long-term debt of 1,623.123 million dollars). Calculated EBITDA (operating income plus DD&A plus impairment, consolidated) is 1,837.5 million dollars for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 against 1,394.0 million dollars for FY2025, so total debt over EBITDA is 0.89x against 0.99x and net debt over EBITDA is 0.62x against 0.72x even though debt rose by 249.3 million dollars. Mechanism: revenue from production rose in the nine months (2,507.9 against 2,076.8 million dollars) on higher realized prices while ex-NCI volumes fell (176,620 against 182,585 BOEPD), and lease operating expenses fell from 605.0 to 436.4 million dollars; the 2025 comparison also carries a 115.0 million dollar impairment that the calculation adds back. Management's own ex-NCI adjusted EBITDA gives a close cross-check: 1,784.8 million dollars for the same twelve months, or 0.92x total debt. Source risk and consequence: the strength of the leverage and cover ratios rests on a high price period and a calculated, NCI-inclusive EBITDA; the free cash flow cushion is small because property additions and dry hole costs of 1,333.0 million dollars absorb most of the 1,517.6 million dollars of operating cash flow, and the balance sheet carries claims outside the debt figure (operating leases, asset retirement obligations, pension and retiree medical, commitments). The metrics therefore support a view of low financial leverage with good near-term liquidity and no note maturity until May 2029, but not a view of covenant headroom, instrument seniority or guarantor coverage, which the sources cannot verify.

fields.value: MURPHY OIL CORP is an independent, publicly listed oil and gas exploration and production company with no sponsor, no controlling owner identified in the sources and no acquisition or leveraged transaction driving the credit view. The decision drivers are therefore the operating model and recent change, not transaction structure. Evidence: crude oil and condensate is 86.1 percent of nine-month 2026 revenue from production, no commodity derivative contracts were in place at September 30, 2026, and realized prices rose sharply on the year (for example United States onshore crude at 86.48 dollars per barrel in Q3 2026 against 65.48 dollars in Q3 2025) while total hydrocarbon production fell 7 percent in Q3 2026 and 3 percent in nine months 2026, which management attributes mainly to lower Gulf of America volumes (natural decline) and to the timing of new onshore wells (10-Q Q3 page:34-36). Risk mechanic: an oil-weighted, unhedged revenue base converts price moves almost directly into cash flow, so the 2026 earnings recovery is a price result with lower volumes; sustaining production requires continuing capital in decline-prone Gulf of America fields (about half of nine-month revenue is United States offshore) while the company also funds exploration and appraisal in Côte d'Ivoire, Vietnam and the Gulf of America. Credit implication: leverage and liquidity are currently strong (CP-1 handoff), but they depend on commodity prices and on management choosing to keep exploration and shareholder returns within cash flow; the sources show that discretion being exercised conservatively on buybacks and with a refinancing that extended maturities, but they do not show the covenant or indenture limits that would constrain distributions or new debt. Credit-relevant change in the period: the January 2026 refinancing (500.0 million dollars of 6.500% notes due 2034, 227.5 million dollars of 2027 and 2028 notes redeemed, revolver upsized to 2.0 billion dollars and extended to January 2031), the first oil at Lac Da Vang in Vietnam with an 83.9 million dollar finance lease for its floating storage vessel, raised 2026 production guidance, and an October 2026 drillship agreement worth approximately 225 million to 325 million dollars gross. The view is limited by missing ownership percentages, customer concentration and capital allocation plan terms (see Gaps).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MURPHY OIL CORP is a financially conservative but price-exposed oil producer, and its credit is sound today. The strongest support is low leverage (total debt of USD 1,634.4 million is 0.89x calculated last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million), liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million and no note maturing before May 2029. The weakest point is that crude oil supplies 86.1 percent of revenue with no commodity derivatives in place, while exploration, development and a new drillship commitment absorb most operating cash flow, leaving little after dividends. What decides the outcome is the oil price and management's willingness to cut discretionary spending and buybacks when it falls; the covenant and indenture limits that would bound that discretion are not in the sources.

fields.value: Rationale. Evidence: MURPHY OIL CORP has total debt of USD 1,634.4 million, net debt of USD 1,134.1 million, cash of USD 500.3 million, calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million, interest paid of USD 86.3 million and cash plus undrawn committed capacity of USD 2,499.9 million, with the nearest note maturity in May 2029 [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: those figures come from a period when United States onshore crude realized USD 86.48 per barrel in Q3 2026 against USD 65.48 in Q3 2025, on an unhedged, oil-weighted revenue base whose volumes fell 7 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A Company and operating model: Pricing; Hedging; Volume and mix]. Credit implication: near-term default risk is low on the reported figures, because leverage, liquidity and the maturity profile give a large buffer; the risk sits in how the company behaves if prices fall, which depends on contract terms the sources do not provide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Category: Analyst Interpretation. MURPHY OIL CORP is a low-leverage, well-funded but oil-price-exposed producer whose creditworthiness depends on keeping discretionary spending and shareholder returns inside cash flow. Basis: [CP-1 Financial base view] and [CP-1A Governance, capital allocation and disclosure behaviour].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the company's leverage is low and has fallen even though debt rose. Total debt was USD 1,385.1 million at December 31, 2025 and USD 1,634.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 249.3 million from a USD 500.0 million notes issue, a USD 83.9 million finance lease and the repayment of USD 227.5 million of notes and the USD 100.0 million revolver draw, while calculated EBITDA rose from USD 1,394.0 million (FY2025) to USD 1,837.5 million (LTM Q3 2026), so total debt over EBITDA moved from 0.99x to 0.89x [CP-1 Debt stack; Chart data: leverage]. The management-basis cross-check gives 0.92x on adjusted EBITDA attributable to Murphy of USD 1,784.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the improvement is a price result. Revenue from production rose to USD 2,507.9 million for nine months 2026 from USD 2,076.8 million, with realized prices up about a third and production down 3 percent, and lease operating costs fell on lower Gulf of America workovers, which management itself describes as partly offset by activity elsewhere [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model: Cost structure; Management explanation of costs]. Part of the cost gain may not repeat, and none of the price gain is protected, because crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and there were no commodity derivatives at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, free cash flow is modest. Calculated free cash flow (operating cash flow less property additions and dry hole costs) was USD 184.6 million for nine months 2026, which after USD 150.5 million of dividends and USD 21.2 million of distributions to the minority holder of MP Gulf of Mexico, LLC leaves USD 12.9 million; management's own adjusted free cash flow was negative USD 32.2 million for the same period, excluding the minority share [CP-1 Free cash flow and shareholder distributions]. Cash still rose by USD 123.1 million because operating cash flow exceeded investing outflow by USD 155.9 million, while financing used USD 32.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, maturities and liquidity are comfortable. No note matures until May 2029 (USD 117.6 million), followed by USD 600.0 million in October 2032, USD 500.0 million in February 2034 and USD 339.8 million in December 2042; the USD 2.0 billion revolver matures January 2, 2031 and is undrawn apart from USD 0.4 million of letters of credit [CP-1 Chart data: debt maturities; Liquidity]. The 2026 refinancing moved the company from a revolver and shorter notes to this profile.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, claims outside the debt figure are large. Asset retirement obligations are USD 1,065.4 million, operating lease liabilities USD 653.8 million, and net pension and retiree medical liabilities were USD 195.8 million at December 31, 2025, before commitments of USD 1,648.0 million at that date and a new drillship agreement of about USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross from the first quarter of 2027 [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Adding the first three to total debt gives USD 3,549.3 million, or 1.93x calculated LTM EBITDA (see Calculations).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, creditor protections are unverified. The previous revolver's tests were a maximum leverage ratio of 3.25x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.50x before an investment grade ratings date, and a 60 percent maximum debt to total capitalization after it; the amended facility's terms, the indentures and the ratings are not supplied, and which test applies is unknown [CP-1 Covenants and definitions; CP-0 Gaps]. The mechanical distance to the stated levels is wide (see Calculations) but is not covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Low leverage is a documentary result: total debt is USD 1,634.4 million against calculated LTM EBITDA of USD 1,837.5 million, and net debt is 0.62x (Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the characterisation) [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 2,499.9 million of cash and undrawn capacity, a revolver to January 2031 and no note before May 2029 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity; Chart data: debt maturities]. Operating cash flow was USD 1,517.6 million for nine months 2026, 52.0 percent above nine months 2025, and calculated LTM EBITDA covers interest paid 21.29x (Documentary Fact for the cash flow, Analyst Interpretation for the cover) [CP-1 Calculations]. Asset base: proved reserves of 730.0 million barrels of oil equivalent at December 31, 2025, about 10.6 years of 2025 production, spread across Eagle Ford Shale, Gulf of America, Tupper Montney, Kaybob Duvernay, Canada offshore and Vietnam, with 43 percent undeveloped (Documentary Fact for reserves, Analyst Interpretation for diversification) [CP-1A Company and operating model: United States assets; Canada assets; Reserves and replacement]. Capital allocation flexibility: buybacks fell from USD 301.4 million in 2024 to USD 102.6 million in 2025 and USD 0.8 million in nine months 2026, which favors creditors, and no related-party leakage, creditor-adverse transaction or sponsor is documented (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading) [CP-1A Governance, capital allocation and disclosure behaviour]. Disclosure quality: quarterly reconciliations of non-GAAP measures and a covenant compliance statement each quarter (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Unhedged oil exposure: crude oil is 86.1 percent of revenue and no commodity derivatives were in place at September 30, 2026; a 10 percent lower oil price on nine-month volumes would have cut revenue and EBITDA by about USD 215.9 million, or 14.0 percent of nine-month calculated EBITDA, before any cost offset (Documentary Fact for the exposure, Analyst Interpretation for the arithmetic) [CP-1A Hedging; Revenue streams]. Thin cash cushion after investment and dividends, as described above (Documentary Fact for the amounts) [CP-1 Free cash flow]. Concentration and decline: United States offshore supplies 50.2 percent of nine-month revenue, and production including the minority share fell 7 percent in Q3 2026, mostly on Gulf of America volumes (Documentary Fact for the percentages, Management Language for the cause) [CP-1A Geographic revenue mix; Volume and mix]. Discretionary, high-risk spending: exploration expense was USD 155.2 million for nine months 2026, including USD 86.7 million of unsuccessful well costs, and the drillship agreement adds a contracted element from 2027 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Cost structure; Transaction summary]. Claims outside debt, including asset retirement obligations equal to about 65 percent of total debt (Analyst Interpretation, calculated) [CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure]. Unverified creditor terms: covenants, indentures, ratings, ownership percentages and customer concentration are missing (Insufficient Information; each missing datapoint is listed under Gaps) [CP-0 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps]. Perimeter: the minority holder takes a share of Gulf of America cash flow, 13.5 percent of consolidated nine-month 2026 net income, and releases and filings use different perimeters (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model: MP GOM subsidiary].
